entities.summary: Al-Humaydi, a renowned Shafi'i jurisprudence scholar and Shaykh of the al-Haram, played a pivotal role in the Islamic Golden Age. Born in the 8th century CE, Al-Humaydi studied under the guidance of Imam Shafi'i himself, solidifying his position as a leading expert in Shafi'i jurisprudence. His scholarship had a lasting impact on the development of Islamic law, as he systematized and codified the Shafi'i madhhab. Al-Humaydi's teachings were widely disseminated, influencing a generation of scholars and clergy. His contributions to Islamic jurisprudence have endured for centuries, shaping the religious and legal practices of Muslims worldwide. A testament to his enduring legacy is the continued reverence for his majlis, where scholars would gather to engage in debates and discussions on Islamic law and theology. Through his meticulous scholarship and unwavering commitment to the Shafi'i tradition, Al-Humaydi left an indelible mark on the intellectual landscape of the Islamic world.

entities.summary: Al-Humaydi, ʻAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, was a renowned Shafi'i jurisprudence scholar and Shaykh of the al-Haram in Medina, Arabia. Born in the 8th century CE, he studied under the great Imam Shafi'i himself, who is considered one of the most influential figures in Islamic jurisprudence. Al-Humaydi's significance lies in his role as a transmitter of Shafi'i's teachings, and his contributions to the development of Shafi'i jurisprudence in the 9th century CE. His work had a lasting impact on the Islamic world, shaping the legal and intellectual landscape of the region for centuries to come. As a testament to his scholarly prowess, al-Humaydi's name is still invoked in Islamic legal scholarship today.
